summary: Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indologist. He earned a PhD from Leipzig and habilitated at Vienna under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in Madras and India, and held a chair at Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) studied at Polytechnikum Riga and worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. In 1881, he was a professor of economics and lecturer in Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.
Eugen Prym (1843–1913) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Bonn from circa 1860 to 1867 and held a post there from circa 1869 to 1913.

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under August Schleicher (ca. 1862–1868) and served as a professor at the University of Jena from circa 1872 to 1923.

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held posts at the University of Pennsylvania, Johns Hopkins University, and Yale University (Lecturer on Pāli, ~1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is an art historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. He taught at the University of Chicago and is the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University.
Eugeni d'Ors (1881–1954) was a philosopher. He studied at the University of Barcelona (ca. 1897–1903) and the Universidad Central (ca. 1903–1905), where he later held a post.

Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck (1913–2003) was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1932 to 1937. He later served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983, succeeding C. C. Berg.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a Polish scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1919–1924), where he also held a post (~1934–1939), before working at Toruń and heading Indology at the University of Warsaw (~1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf (1801–1852) was a French Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as Secretary of the Société Asiatique and held a teaching post at the Collège de France from 1832 to 1852.
Eugène Jacquet (1811–1838) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat from circa 1828 to 1832 and under Eugène Burnouf from circa 1832 to 1838.

Eugène Obermiller (1901–1935) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Dondub Buddhayin, and served as Section Secretary at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1935).

Eugène Tisserant (1884–1972) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1904–1907), and the École du Louvre (~1905–1907).

Eun Hino (born 1981) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree and served as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo. She later became an assistant professor and then an associate professor at Musashino University.
Eun Maeda (1857–1930) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He taught Kozui Otani and served as president of both Toyo University and Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, under Padmanabh S. Jaini, served as an assistant professor at the University of Michigan, and joined Seoul National University in 2004.
Eunyoung Choe (born 1968) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies at Korea University and held an HK professor post at Geumgang University, attested in 2013–2015.

Eva K. Neumaier (born 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2006, she was Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary and Professor Emeritus and former department chair at the University of Alberta.

Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay (born 1937) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin. She held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1992.

Eva Tichy (born 1951) is a linguist and Indologist. She earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nuremberg, completed her habilitation at Marburg, and held the Chair of Indo-European Studies at the University of Freiburg from 1993 to 2017.
